newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures pare gains, still end mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures pare gains, still end mostly higher.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures pared early gains but still ended mostly higher Thursday in lackluster trade, helped by a firmer cash and some technical buying though many stayed sidelined ahead of the first.
November climbed 4.1 cents to close at $2.137 per million British thermal units. December settled 3.2 cents higher at $2.33. Most others ended steady to up 1.5 cents.

"I still like it, but next month we need a good cool front to come in. In this dead zone (shoulder period), November could be pressured back to $2, but I think there will be a lot of people ready to scoop it up," said one Texas trader.

While eastern storage injections are likely to slow next month as caverns fill, traders said favorable cash-to-futures spreads should keep production area rates relatively high and pick up some of the slack. But most agreed it will take some early heating loads to really tighten the balance and rally the market from here.
Technically, traders pegged November support in the $2.00 area, with resistance at today's high of $2.18 and then at the recent high of $2.305.

Cash sources said September Gulf Coast prices firmed a couple of cents Thursday to the low-to-mid $1.90s. October Gulf Coast gas notionally was talked little changed in the low-to-mid $1.80s. Oct Midcon gas also held relatively steady in the mid-$1.70s. New York city gate gas for October delivery was pegged modestly higher in the $2.10-2.15 area.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip rose 1.2 cents to $2.085. NYMEX said 25,634 contracts traded, up slightly from Wednesday's revised tally of 23,686.
NYMEX October Permian natgas expired 2.5 cents higher at $1.695, while deferreds were untraded. NYMEX said 131 Permian lots traded, up from Wednesday's total of 58.
On the KCBT, November settled 4.5 cents higher at $1.89, while most deferreds ended up by one to two cents. The November East/West spread narrowed by 0.4 cent to 24.7 cents (NYMEX premium).
